**Lane:** app · **Complexity:** 2 · **Model:** codex · **Depends on:** KM-104 · **Serializes with:** KM-130 (both edit `apps/control/src/composition/human/{matrix,handlers}.ts`)
**Plan context (pinned):** [M1 plan](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/plans/2026-10-01-002-refactor-external-m1-thin-path-plan.md) · [contracts](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/contracts.md) · [roster and graph](https://github.com/aiur-team/khala/blob/reset/m1-external-plan/docs/build/m1/roster.md)
**Exclusive write surfaces:**
- `apps/control/src/composition/human/{handlers,matrix,production,room-send-routes,device-admission-routes,matrix-event-receipt}.ts`
- `apps/control/src/composition/agent/production-bootstrap.ts` (import line only)

## Outcome

1. The existing `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` keeps its request shape. Each response entry is the C3 `Participant`: today's keys plus a mandatory `kind`:
   - humans come from the deterministic account mapping (`kind: 'human'`);
   - agents come from the C3 owner map (`agents/<matrixUserId>`), with `ownerLabel` and `harness` (`kind: 'agent'`);
   - any other member is `{ matrixUserId, displayName, kind: 'unknown' }`.

   An unknown member never fails the response; it replaces today's `unavailable` result. Resolution no longer uses `createAgentIdentityDirectory`, `createOwnerRoomIndex` or `createAgentBindingStore`. There is no new route and no GET method (reconciliation A2).
2. `displayName` is the member's Matrix display name from `joined_members`, falling back to the user id (C3, C4).
3. Each human's Matrix display name is set to `ownerFirstName(verifiedEmail)` (C4) when that human mints a browser session, so human labels read `Kevin` instead of the opaque user id.
4. `createMatrixBrowserSenderVerifier` and `BrowserSenderVerifier` live in `composition/human/browser-sender.ts`, so KM-123 can delete `room-send-routes.ts`.

## Context and evidence

- Plan U6 approach: "Participant attribution reads human mappings plus the `agents/` owner map (KTD9). An unknown member maps to `unknown`; it does not fail the history read. Today `matrix.ts:387-475` fails the whole read." KTD9 replaces `createAgentIdentityDirectory` and `createAgentBindingStore`.
- Today the route is POST-only with a `userIds` body: `apps/control/src/composition/human/handlers.ts:352-388`.
  - With `roomId` it requires a browser device proof (`verifyBrowserSender`, `:375-377`).
  - It then calls `resolveRoomParticipants` (`matrix.ts:387-475`).
  - That function backfills agents from the binding store (`:425-454`) and returns `unavailable` when any user is unresolved (`:455`, `:472-474`).
- The web caller is `apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.ts:345-372`. It POSTs `{userIds, roomId, deviceId, matrixAccessToken}` and requires the legacy entry keys exactly: `matrixUserId, participantId, ownerId, displayName[, kind]` (`:354-356`). The new `ownerLabel`/`harness` keys and `kind: 'unknown'` entries fail that exact-key parser, so KM-135 (which depends on this ticket) updates it. Between this merge and KM-135, a room with an agent or unknown member shows the browser's existing "participants unavailable" path, as it does today for unresolved members.
- The verifier lives at `apps/control/src/composition/human/room-send-routes.ts:43-82`. Its importers are:
  - `human/handlers.ts:17` (type);
  - `human/production.ts:13` and `:71-76`;
  - `human/device-admission-routes.ts:5` (type);
  - `human/matrix-event-receipt.ts:3`;
  - `agent/production-bootstrap.ts:19` (alongside other `room-send-routes` exports);
  - `human/room-send-routes.test.ts:9` and `:193-218`.
- The control store returns `ControlRead = absent | record | unavailable` (`packages/contracts/src/messaging/control-store.ts:21-24`). Keys with `%` are hashed to a safe physical key by the adapter (`apps/control/src/runtime/control-store.ts:148-150`), so the C3 key needs no extra encoding.
- The room member list comes from `/_matrix/client/v3/rooms/<room>/joined_members`, which returns `{ joined: { <userId>: { display_name?, avatar_url? } } }`. It is already read at `matrix.ts:396-402`.

## Scope

- Rewire `resolveRoomParticipants` (the POST room-scoped branch) off the agent stores and onto the C3 owner map, returning C3 `Participant` entries with `unknown` instead of failing.
- Add `kind: 'human'` and the Matrix display name to the non-room POST branch (`resolveParticipants`) entries.
- Set each human's own Matrix display name at session mint (C4, step 5a).
- Move the browser-sender verifier into its own file and update its importers.
- Tests for all of the above.

## Non-goals

- Deleting routes, `room-send-routes.ts`, `inspectRoomSenderDevices`, `inspectOwnerDeviceKey`, `channelCreateFor` or the `agent-bootstrap` imports at `matrix.ts:2-4`. Those belong to KM-123, because `inspectRoomSenderDevices` (`matrix.ts:551-634`) still uses them.
- Updating the browser caller's exact-key parser (`apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.ts:345-372`) and rendering C3 participants: KM-135.
- Any new route or HTTP method on the participants path (reconciliation A2: none).
- Writing the owner map. KM-132 writes `agents/<matrixUserId>` at confirm.
- The `history: 'full'` refusals and `history_visibility`: KM-130.

## Contract and invariants

C3 (verbatim):

```ts
export type AgentOwnerRecord = { matrixUserId: string; ownerId: string; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness; label: string; createdAt: string };
```

> Participants: there is **no new route**. The existing `POST /api/human/messaging/participants` (`apps/control/src/composition/human/handlers.ts:31`, `:352-388` at `5db209cc`) keeps its request shape (`{ userIds, roomId?, deviceId?, matrixAccessToken?, targetParticipantIds? }`). Each entry of its `{ participants: [...] }` response keeps today's keys and gains `kind: 'human'|'agent'|'unknown'`, plus `ownerLabel` and `harness` when `kind === 'agent'`:

```ts
export type Participant =
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'human' }
  | { matrixUserId: string; participantId: string; ownerId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'agent'; ownerLabel: string; harness: Harness }
  | { matrixUserId: string; displayName: string; kind: 'unknown' };   // an unknown member never fails the whole response
export type ParticipantsResponse = { participants: Participant[] };
```

> - `displayName` is the member's Matrix display name (C4 human-label rule), falling back to `matrixUserId`.
> - KM-122 implements the augmentation; KM-135 consumes it through the existing caller in `apps/web/src/composition/human/browser-api.ts` (`MATRIX_PARTICIPANTS_PATH` `:53`, `participants.resolve` `:345-372`).

Netlify Blobs key: `agents/<encodeURIComponent(matrixUserId)>`.

C4 (verbatim excerpt):

> `ownerFirstName` is derived from the owner's verified email. … KM-122, KM-132 and KM-135 use this same rule via `ownerFirstName(email)` exported from `packages/contracts/src/m1/participants.ts`, which KM-104 owns.
> - **Human labels come from Matrix display names, everywhere.** When KM-122 mints a browser session, it sets the human's own Matrix display name to `ownerFirstName(verifiedEmail)`: read it first, write only if different. Readers (control participants, browser, KM-143 agent intake) use the display name and fall back to the user id localpart.

Invariants:
- The route path, methods (POST only) and request validation (`handlers.ts:360-377`) are unchanged.
- An owner-map read error, a corrupt record or `record.matrixUserId !== userId` makes that member `unknown`. It never fails the response.
- No access token or store key appears in any response body.

### Worked example

POST `/api/human/messaging/participants` from `owner_kevin`'s browser, body (request shape unchanged):

```json
{ "userIds": ["<ownerMatrixUserId('owner_kevin','khala.local')>", "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local", "@stranger:khala.local"],
  "roomId": "!r:khala.local", "deviceId": "<browser device>", "matrixAccessToken": "<browser token>" }
```

Synapse `joined_members` returns:

```json
{ "joined": {
  "<ownerMatrixUserId('owner_kevin','khala.local')>": { "display_name": "Kevin" },
  "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local": { "display_name": "Claude · Kevin" },
  "@stranger:khala.local": {} } }
```

The store record at `agents/%40agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7%3Akhala.local` is:

```json
{ "matrixUserId":"@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local","ownerId":"owner_kevin","ownerLabel":"Kevin","harness":"claude","label":"Claude","createdAt":"2026-10-02T10:00:00Z" }
```

Response 200, in `userIds` order:

```json
{ "participants": [
  { "matrixUserId": "@khala_…:khala.local", "participantId": "human_<40 hex>", "ownerId": "owner_kevin", "displayName": "Kevin", "kind": "human" },
  { "matrixUserId": "@agent-1a2b3c4d-x9y8z7:khala.local", "participantId": "agent_<first 40 hex of sha256(userId)>", "ownerId": "owner_kevin",
    "displayName": "Claude · Kevin", "kind": "agent", "ownerLabel": "Kevin", "harness": "claude" },
  { "matrixUserId": "@stranger:khala.local", "displayName": "@stranger:khala.local", "kind": "unknown" } ] }
```

### Steps

1. **Move the verifier.**
   - Create `browser-sender.ts` containing `BrowserSenderVerifier` and `createMatrixBrowserSenderVerifier`, copied byte-for-byte from `room-send-routes.ts:43-82`.
   - Bring along a local `object()` helper (copy of `room-send-routes.ts:19`) and `import { ownerMatrixUserId } from './matrix-identity'`.
   - Delete those lines from `room-send-routes.ts`. Add `import { createMatrixBrowserSenderVerifier, type BrowserSenderVerifier } from './browser-sender';` there, because `:90` and `:114` still use the type.
   - Point every importer listed in Context at `./browser-sender` (or `../human/browser-sender`). In `production-bootstrap.ts:19`, split the import so `createLazyRoomSendRoutes` and `createRoomSendRoutes` still come from `room-send-routes`.
2. **Move the verifier test.** Move the `it('verifies the transient browser Matrix token …')` block (`room-send-routes.test.ts:193-218`) into `browser-sender.test.ts`, together with the `principal` and `human` fixtures it needs (`:13-21`). Remove `createMatrixBrowserSenderVerifier` from the import at `:9`.
3. **Add the owner-map reader in `matrix.ts`.**
   - Add imports `agentOwnerRecordKey`, `decodeAgentOwnerRecord`, `type AgentOwnerRecord` and `type Participant` from `'@khala/contracts/m1/participants'`.
   - Inside `createMatrixHumanServices`, next to `participantFor` (`:188`), add `readAgentOwner(userId, call): Promise<AgentOwnerRecord | null | 'unavailable'>`:
     - `absent` → `null`;
     - `record` whose decode is ok and whose `matrixUserId === userId` → the record;
     - anything else, including a throw → `'unavailable'`.
   - Add `agentParticipantId(userId)` → `` `agent_${createHash('sha256').update(userId).digest('hex').slice(0, 40)}` as ParticipantId ``.
4. **Retype the result.** Replace `MatrixParticipant` (`matrix.ts:69-75`) with an alias of the C3 `Participant` (`export type MatrixParticipant = Participant;`), so `resolveParticipants` and `resolveRoomParticipants` (`:59-66`) return C3 entries. Fix `participantFor` (`:188-197`) to add `kind: 'human'`. The other user of `participantFor` (`:571`, `inspectRoomSenderDevices`) only reads `ownerId`; keep it compiling, and narrow with `kind === 'human'` where the type demands it.
5. **Rewire POST `resolveRoomParticipants`.** Keep `:387-402` (membership plus the bounded `joined_members` read) unchanged. Replace `:403-474` with:
   1. For each `userId`, compute `display`: `joined[userId].display_name` when it is a string of 1..256 chars with no `[\u0000-\u001f\u007f-\u009f]`, otherwise `null`.
   2. `participantFor(userId)` matches → `{ ...human, displayName: display ?? userId, kind: 'human' }`.
   3. Otherwise a `readAgentOwner` record → `{ matrixUserId: userId, participantId: agentParticipantId(userId), ownerId: rec.ownerId, displayName: display ?? userId, kind: 'agent', ownerLabel: rec.ownerLabel, harness: rec.harness }`.
   4. Otherwise (no record, `'unavailable'`, or not in `joined`) → `{ matrixUserId: userId, displayName: display ?? userId, kind: 'unknown' }`. Never return `{ kind: 'unavailable' }` for an unresolved member (C3).
   5. Accept `targetParticipantIds` but ignore it, with a one-line comment saying owner-map agents are not indexed by participant id.
   6. Return `{ kind:'ok', participants }` in `userIds` order.
   - Remove the `createAgentIdentityDirectory` import (`:5`) and the now-unused `canReadIdentity` helper. Keep `:2-4`, because `inspectRoomSenderDevices` still uses them.
6. **Non-room POST `resolveParticipants`** (`:380-385`): keep the 100-entry and duplicate checks. Map each `userId` to `participantFor(userId)` with `kind: 'human'` (display name = user id; there is no room to read `joined_members` from), else `{ matrixUserId: userId, displayName: userId, kind: 'unknown' }`. It no longer returns `unavailable` for an unknown user.
6a. **Human display name (C4, reconciliation A3).** The server cannot apply `ownerFirstName` to *other* humans: no store record maps `ownerId` to an email. `auth/principal.ts:60-65` stores only issuer and subject, and `auth/provisioning.ts:31-33` stores only the account id. So each human's own first name is published as their Matrix display name when they mint a session. Matrix then carries it to every reader: this route, the browser, and the agent (KM-143 reads member display names).
   - In `sessions.issue` (`matrix.ts:368-379`), after a successful `login`, compute `name = ownerFirstName(principal.verifiedEmail)`, imported from `@khala/contracts/m1/participants`.
   - `GET /_matrix/client/v3/profile/<userId>/displayname` with the new session token. Only when the response is 404, or `displayname !== name`, send `PUT` to the same path with `{ "displayname": name }`. This avoids a member-event storm, because every PUT re-emits `m.room.member` in all joined rooms.
   - Errors are ignored and never change the `issue` result.
   - The human `displayName` in step 5 then comes from `display_name`, with the user id as fallback for accounts that have not minted a session since.
7. **Handler.** Apart from the step-1 import at `handlers.ts:17`, `handlers.ts:352-388` stays byte-identical: same path, `methods: post`, same request validation. It already returns `{ participants: result.participants }`, which now carries C3 entries.
8. **Rewrite agent tests in `matrix.test.ts`.**
   - Delete the two agent-backfill tests at `:554-570` and `:571-579` and the departed-agent test at `:691-715`.
   - Add a new top-level `describe('room participants (owner map)')`, so KM-123 can delete the whole `'Matrix room sender inventory'` describe later.
   - Update the `resolveParticipants` expectations at `:333`, `:480` and `:485` to the C3 shape (`kind: 'human'`; the unknown user at `:485` now yields `{ kind:'ok', participants:[{ matrixUserId, displayName, kind:'unknown' }] }`).
   - Remove imports that are now unused.

## Test scenarios

`apps/control/src/composition/human/matrix.test.ts`, new describe `room participants (owner map)`. Use `memoryStore()` and write the owner record with `store.compareAndSet({ key: agentOwnerRecordKey(id), expectedRevision: null, operationId: 'op', next: { value: record, expiresAt: null } })`.
1. Covers U6 (agent). The worked example → `ok` with exactly the three entries in `userIds` order; the agent entry has `kind:'agent'`, `ownerLabel:'Kevin'`, `harness:'claude'`; the human entry has `displayName:'Kevin'`.
2. Covers U6 (unknown). A member with no owner record → `kind:'unknown'` and `displayName` equal to its user id (no `display_name`). The result is still `ok`.
3. A store whose `read` throws for the agent key → that member is `unknown`, and the result is `ok`.
4. A record whose `matrixUserId` differs from the key's user → `unknown`.
5. Membership 403 → `{kind:'forbidden'}`. `joined_members` 500 → `unavailable` with `localDiagnostic.stage === 'joined_members'`.
6. A `display_name` containing `\u0007` → the human `displayName` falls back to the user id.
7. `targetParticipantIds` is ignored (passing one changes nothing).
8. Existing test `'uses the verified browser bearer across fresh Control instances…'` (`:641`) still passes, with expectations updated only for the added `kind`/`displayName` fields.
9. `issue` for `verifiedEmail: 'kevin.weaver2@gmail.com'`:
   - the profile GET returns `{displayname:'khala_x'}` → exactly one PUT, with body `{"displayname":"Kevin"}`;
   - the profile GET returns `{displayname:'Kevin'}` → no PUT;
   - the PUT returns 500 → `issue` is still `ok`.
   Update the existing `issue` test at `:392` so its fetch fake answers the profile calls.
10. Non-room `resolveParticipants(['@khala_bad:elsewhere.test'])` → `ok` with one `unknown` entry.

`apps/control/src/composition/human/handlers.test.ts`: existing POST tests (`:300-386`) and the method-shape assertion (`:91-101`, `[MATRIX_PARTICIPANTS_PATH, ['POST']]`) pass unchanged.

`apps/control/src/composition/human/browser-sender.test.ts`: the moved verifier test passes unchanged.

## Risks and stop conditions

- If `pnpm typecheck` fails in `tests/e2e/security/relay.test.ts` because of the type change, check first. It casts with `as unknown as MatrixSessionIssuer` at `:88`, so it should not fail. If something else outside `apps/control` breaks, stop and report it. Do not edit `tests/`.
- `apps/web`'s exact-key parser (`browser-api.ts:354-356`) rejects the new keys until KM-135 lands; that is expected. Do not edit `apps/web`.
- If KM-130 has already merged and changed `matrix.ts`, rebase and keep its changes. Do not revert `history_visibility` or the history-refusal edits.
- Stop and ask the Executor if C3 changes. Do not add a GET method, a new route path or a new server-side service (reconciliation A2; plan stop condition).
- Do not add a new store record for emails; the display-name mechanism in step 6a is the Executor's decision (A3).

## Complexity rationale

2: a narrow rewire of one resolver onto the owner map, a session-mint display-name write, and a mechanical file move across seven importers. Keeping the route and request shape unchanged is the main subtlety, and it is fully specified above.
